domain_restrictions: n must be a positive integer (to make 'modulo n' and least nonnegative residue well-defined over {0,...,n-1})
m is an integer satisfying 0 <= m <= n-1
r_k is constrained to be the least nonnegative residue of k*m modulo n, hence r_k lies in {0,...,n-1}
j is an integer satisfying 1 <= j <= n-1
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every positive integer n, for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, define for each k in {1,...,n} the least nonnegative residue r_k of k*m modulo n (so r_k is in {0,...,n-1}). Then for every integer j with 1 <= j <= n-1, the set S_{m,j} = {k in {1,...,n} : r_k >= j} has cardinality at most n-j.
quantifier_order: for all integers m with 0 <= m <= n-1
for all integers j with 1 <= j <= n-1

variables.name: n
variables.role: modulus; also sets the ranges {1,...,n} and {1,...,n-1}

variables.name: k
variables.role: index of residues and elements of the set S_{m,j}

variables.domain: least nonnegative residue in {0,1,...,n-1} of (k*m) mod n
variables.name: r_k
variables.role: computed value depending on m, k, and n

variables.name: j
variables.role: threshold defining membership criterion r_k >= j

variables.name: S_{m,j}
variables.role: set of indices k for which the corresponding residue r_k is at least j

witness_dependencies: r_k depends on n and on the chosen m, and is defined for each k in {1,...,n}
S_{m,j} depends on n and on the chosen m and j, through the membership condition r_k >= j using the previously defined r_k

statement_nl: For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, let r_k be the least nonnegative residue of k*m modulo n for k = 1, ..., n. For each integer j with 1 <= j <= n-1, the set S_{m,j} = {k in {1,...,n} : r_k >= j} has cardinality at most n-j.
